title: U-Space: Uncovering When and Why Uncertainty Arises in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.09087v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are informing decisions with ever-higher stakes. As the consequences of their errors grow, a central question becomes harder to ignore: how much can we trust an individual answer? Yet recognizing when to defer remains difficult because language models can present incorrect conclusions with fluent explanations and an authoritative tone. Uncertainty quantification seeks to address this disconnect by estimating the reliability of individual predictions. However, many existing methods require repeated generations or separately trained components, and their scalar estimates do not reveal where uncertainty arises or how it evolves during reasoning. Recent work has also shown that generation length can be strongly associated with uncertainty estimates and correctness, raising the question of how much of an estimator's predictive power comes from uncertainty-specific information rather than output length alone. translated_title: U-Space：揭示语言模型中不确定性何时以及为何产生
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型正以越来越高的风险影响着各类决策。随着其错误所造成的后果不断加剧，一个核心问题变得越来越难以忽视：我们对模型给出的单个回答能有多少信任？然而，识别何时应当“推迟判断”仍然困难，因为语言模型能够以流利的解释和权威的语气呈现错误的结论。不确定性量化旨在通过估计单个预测的可靠性来解决这种脱节。然而，许多现有方法需要重复生成或单独训练的组件，且其标量化的估计值无法揭示不确定性在何处产生、以及在推理过程中如何演变。近期研究还表明，生成长度可能与不确定性估计和正确性密切相关，这引发了一个问题：估计器的预测能力中，有多少来自不确定性特有的信息，而非仅仅来自输出长度。（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出U-Space方法，旨在揭示语言模型推理过程中不确定性在何时、何处以及为何产生与演变，克服了现有标量化不确定性估计方法无法定位不确定性来源的局限性。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes U-Space, a method that uncovers when, where, and why uncertainty arises and evolves during language model reasoning, addressing the limitations of existing scalar uncertainty estimation methods.
